listenings.text: If you come from agency finance and you sit in front of a board from another industry, there is one thing you have to disarm in the first minute, and it is billings. In our world billings is the total value invoiced to clients, and it can be six or seven times revenue, because most of what we invoice is media that passes straight through us. To a board that has never worked in this industry, a billings number sounds like the size of the company, and if you let that misunderstanding stand you will spend the rest of the meeting correcting it. So say it once, plainly. Billings were four hundred million, revenue was fifty five, and the number that matters for this conversation is the fifty five. Then move on. The same applies to pacing, which everybody in advertising says twenty times a day and nobody outside it understands. If a word only exists inside your industry, define it in six words the first time you use it and never define it again.

What I walked into was a holding company with four subsidiaries, two of which had been acquired eighteen months earlier and had never really been integrated. My formal reporting line was to the group chief executive, who was based in London, and I had a dotted line to the group finance director, who was the person who actually decided things. That distinction cost me about six months to work out. The business units each had their own controller, which sounded sensible on paper and meant in practice that nobody owned a consolidated number. The shared service centre we eventually built was not my idea, and I will say that clearly because people always assume it was. It came from one of the controllers, whose team was doing the same reconciliation four times a month for four different entities.

extra_audio.text: Ines asks Fernando to walk her through a single year in the numbers. Fernando gives the gross margin and the overhead base he started the year with. Fernando explains what happened in February and what he told the board. Fernando says which action bought nothing and which one worked. Ines asks about the write-offs and Fernando names the number he is proud of.
